name: Sonnet global diversification via US-listed ADRs and ETFs
strategy: Domestic sector relative-value: ride confirmed catalyst momentum in biotech/financials while shorting overextended mean-reversion candidates (gold miners, leveraged semis) with hard stops for intraweek discipline.

positions.thesis: Core MSCI EAFE developed-ex-US ETF for broad, low-cost diversification away from US mega-cap AI concentration and away from the whipsaw semis trade.
Novartis (Swiss) ADR -- defensive global pharma exposure, low correlation to US tech/semis volatility.
Rio Tinto (UK/Australia) ADR -- diversified miner giving commodity/EM-demand exposure distinct from tech-driven return streams.
Unilever (UK/Netherlands) ADR -- global consumer staples ballast, defensive counterweight to volatile AI/semis-linked assets.
UK equity ETF for developed-market diversification with limited AI/semis-sector weight.
Mexico ETF -- nearshoring/EM-Americas diversification, low correlation to US mega-cap tech drawdowns.
EM USD sovereign bond ETF -- adds income and a different risk driver (rates/EM credit) to diversify the book's return sources away from equity-momentum/semis bets.

reassessment_note: Week 2 Info Desk (2026-07-25, drip protocol — released items only): The Round-3 book on file (XBI/XLF/KRE momentum longs, GDX/SOXL mean-reversion shorts, TLT ballast) is a domestic sector relative-value book with zero ADR/international content -- it does not match this manager's mandate of global diversification via US-listed ADRs and ETFs. Bringing it back on-mandate: replacing with a developed/EM-ex-US ADR and ETF book spanning Europe, UK, Latin America, Australia and EM sovereign debt, with no US sector-timing bets and no semis exposure. The newest info (continued sharp semis/AI-infra volatility -- SOXL -13.14% on 07-24 alone after a mid-week bounce, SMH -9.33% 1m) argues for staying out of leveraged US tech/semis mean-reversion bets given how whippy that trade has been, reinforcing the case for a calmer, defensively-tilted international book here instead.
novelty: This book's return driver is developed-market defensive/staples/healthcare ADRs plus EM sovereign bonds across Europe, the UK, Latin America and Australia -- entirely disjoint in symbols and driver from the domestic-sector-rotation book previously on file, and also disjoint from the Round-2 book's EM-tech/Asia set (EEM/TSM/ASML/EWZ/EWJ/BABA/INDA/SQQQ), giving 0% same-direction gross-weight overlap with Round 2.
